questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Why can the 68-95-99.7 rule be used to find a 95% range for simulated sample proportions from large random samples?
questions.prompt_markup: Why can the 68-95-99.7 rule be used to find a 95% range for simulated sample proportions from large random samples?

choices.text: The population values must be normal, even though the sample proportions themselves are not normal.
For large enough samples their distribution is approximately normal, so about 95% fall within 2 SD of the mean.
Sample proportions are exactly normal for every sample size, so the rule needs no conditions at all.
The 68-95-99.7 rule applies to every histogram, whatever its shape, so no check is needed.

questions.correct_answer: For large enough samples their distribution is approximately normal, so about 95% fall within 2 SD of the mean.
questions.grading_note: The normal model is an approximation that works when the simulated distribution is mound-shaped and symmetric. The others require the population to be normal, claim exact normality for every sample size, or apply the rule to any shape.
